_about: Bennet Tyler (1783-1858), president of Dartmouth and first president of the Theological Institute of Connecticut (East Windsor), the chief opponent of Taylor's New Haven theology: Letters on the Origin and Progress of the New Haven Theology (New York, 1837), New England Revivals (Boston, 1846), The Sufferings of Christ Confined to his Human Nature (Hartford, 1847) and his posthumous Lectures on Theology, with a memoir by Nahum Gale (Boston: J. E. Tilton, 1859; a Google scan, and Google asks for non-commercial use). His Nettleton books are on the asahel-nettleton shelf. Internet Archive OCR, raw and unconverted; each title page read before listing.
